NC-C.mechanism_specific_claim: A distributed fluid-control network in which local drainage elements autonomously reallocate flow in response to predicted (not current) occlusion, maintaining a target global intracranial pressure while preventing overload of surviving paths. The dual safety invariant (global ICP preservation AND surviving-path overload prevention) is the potentially novel element.

state_variables: Segment occlusion probability (P_occl_i, from flow/pressure trend)
frozen_control_law.occlusion_probability_calculation: Bayesian update from flow decline rate + pressure gradient change. P(occlusion within 6h | current trends) = posterior from exponential failure model with flow-decline covariate.
frozen_control_law.transition_rule: IF P_occl_i > threshold THEN: (1) reduce q_i to 50% (prevent overload of segment i), (2) redistribute (q_i * 0.5) to neighboring segments j where P_occl_j < threshold AND p_j < p_max (overload invariant), (3) maintain sum(q_j) = Q_target (global ICP invariant).
frozen_control_law.flow_redistribution_rule: Greedy: assign excess flow to lowest-pressure, lowest-risk neighbor first. Respect p_j < p_max for all j.
frozen_control_law.surviving_path_overload_invariant: p_j < p_max for all active segments j at all times
frozen_control_law.dual_safety_invariant: Global ICP maintained AND no surviving path overloaded. BOTH must hold simultaneously.
